subject: Maths
title: Mean, median, mode and range
subtitle: Statistics · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the mean, median, mode and range from a set of data.

key_vocab.definition: The mean is the sum of values divided by the count. The median is the middle value when data is ordered. The mode is the most frequent value.
The mean is the sum of values divided by the count. The median is the middle value when data is ordered. The mode is the most frequent value.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the mean, median, mode and range from a set of data.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content:
mean -- The mean is the sum of values divided by the count. The median is the middle value when data is ordered. The mode is the most frequent value.
mode -- The mean is the sum of values divided by the count. The median is the middle value when data is ordered. The mode is the most frequent value.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Mean = total ÷ number of values. Median = middle value (or mean of two middle values for even counts).
Mean = ∑x ÷ n
Sum all values and divide by how many there are

Key examples:
  ✓ Mean of 2, 4, 6 = 12 ÷ 3 = 4  (sum ÷ count)
  ✓ Median of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 = 7  (middle value)
  ✓ Mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7 = 3  (most frequent)
  ✗ Median of 2, 4, 6, 8 = 6  (should be (4+6)÷2 = 5)
  ✗ Range of 3, 7, 10, 2 = 10  (range = 10 - 2 = 8)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – finding the mean
  Find the mean of 5, 8, 3, 12, 7.
  Sum = 5 + 8 + 3 + 12 + 7 = 35
  Count = 5
  Mean = 35 ÷ 5 = 7
  Mean = 7
  (Add all values then divide by how many there are.)

Example 2 – finding the median
  Find the median of 9, 3, 7, 1, 5, 8, 2.
  Order: 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9
  7 values, middle is the 4th
  Median = 5
  Median = 5
  (Always put the data in order first.)

sections.title: Range and comparing data
sections.content:
Find the range. Compare the data sets.

(a) 5, 8, 12, 3, 15
(b) 22, 25, 21, 28, 24
(c) Set A: mean 50, range 20. Set B: mean 50, range 5. Which is more consistent?
(d) 100, 102, 98, 105, 95

sections.title: From frequency tables
sections.content:
Calculate the mean from each frequency table.

(a) Score 1(f=3), 2(f=5), 3(f=7), 4(f=4), 5(f=1)
(b) Goals 0(f=4), 1(f=6), 2(f=3), 3(f=2)
(c) Shoe size 5(f=2), 6(f=5), 7(f=8), 8(f=3), 9(f=2)
(d) Hours 0(f=1), 1(f=4), 2(f=6), 3(f=5), 4(f=4)

sections.title: Mixed averages
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Mean of 5 numbers is 8. Sum?
(b) 6 numbers have mean 10. A 7th number (17) is added. New mean?
(c) Data: 3, 5, x, 9, 11. Mean is 7. Find x.
(d) Median of 2, 5, x, 12, 15 is 8. Find x.
(e) Range is 12, lowest value is 5. Highest value?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values
✗ The median of 2, 4, 6, 8 is 6
✓ The mode can be more than one value
✗ Range = highest value
✓ For an even set, the median is the mean of the two middle values
